journal_new.title: Effect of fullerene C60, diamond, and graphene oxide on oncolytic properties of herpes simplex virus type 1 against hepatocellular carcinoma
journal_new.abstract: Background Oncolytic viruses selectively target cancer cells but have their virulence or latency factors removed, which reduces their therapeutic efficacy. Oncolytic viruses represent a new tool in the cancer therapy, but their effectiveness depends on efficient delivery before recognition by the immune system. The aim of this study was to determine the effect of fullerene C 60 , diamond, and graphene oxide nanoparticles on the oncolytic properties of modified herpes simplex virus type 1 (+ GFP, -γ34.5, -UL39). We hypothesised that carbon nanoparticles facilitate entry of the oncolytic virus into cancer cells via nanopores and enhance cancer cell death. Results Fullerene and diamond nanoparticles were biocompatible with cancer cells after 24 h of incubation. Graphene oxide at concentrations of 50 and 100 mg/L inhibited cellular metabolic activity. HSV-1 induced a dose-dependent cytopathic effect (CPE) including cell rounding and syncytium formation, which were more pronounced in C3A cells than in SNU-449 cells. Fullerene and diamond showed aggregation in the presence of HSV-1. The Combination of the virus with graphene oxide and nanodiamond nanoparticles caused a physical reduction in the size of the virus particles. ND caused the best increase in the number of HSV-1 copies in the cells and culture medium of the C3A line, while C 60 increased viral DNA in the SNU-449 culture medium. Carbon nanoparticle-modified HSV-1 entered cells, expressed green fluorescent protein, and reduced mitochondrial activity without increasing lactate dehydrogenase leakage into the extracellular environment. Graphene oxide and diamond reduced expression of icp27 , vp16 , gD , casp3 , and bcl2 , as well as the HSV-1 receptor hvem at the mRNA level. Carbon nanoparticles kept the virus inside the cells, which was associated with reduced vp16 expression. Moreover, the addition of C 60 and diamond to HSV-1 resulted in an increase in viral antigen levels in cells. Conclusion Carbon-based nanomaterials differentially influenced HSV-1 DNA levels, viral antigen expression, and cellular responses in hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines. These effects depended on both the nanomaterial and the investigated cell line. Although the findings suggest that fullerene C 60 and nanodiamonds warrant further investigation as potential components of oncolytic virus delivery strategies, the present results do not establish enhanced production of infectious viral progeny or synergistic oncolytic activity.

journal_new.title: Surface Adsorbates Suppress Low-Frequency Noise for Shallow Nitrogen-Vacancy Centers
journal_new.abstract: Shallow nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are promising nanoscale quantum sensors, yet their coherence is strongly limited by surface-induced noise. Surface adsorbates are widely believed to be a major source of decoherence. Here, we test this assumption by characterizing shallow single NV centers under ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) conditions, where the diamond surface is kept free of adsorbates, and comparing their behavior to ambient conditions. Surprisingly, we observe a ∼ 4 × reduction in the Hahn echo coherence time T 2 in UHV. By combining Hahn echo measurements in the single-quantum and double-quantum (DQ) bases, we separate contributions from different noise sources and find that both electric and magnetic noise are enhanced in UHV. In contrast, T 1 measurements reveal an increased DQ T 1 in UHV, indicating suppressed electric field noise in the ∼ 100 MHz frequency regime. These results point to a modification of the surface noise spectrum upon adsorbate removal, with different frequency regimes arising from distinct microscopic mechanisms. Specifically, we find that the low-frequency noise is consistent with increased surface charge in UHV that can be compensated by surface adsorbates in ambient conditions. Our findings highlight a complex and previously underappreciated role of surface adsorbates in shaping the noise environment of shallow NV centers, with important implications for nanoscale quantum sensing.

journal_new.title: First-principles cumulant approach to the vibronic structure of spin defects
journal_new.abstract: Color centers in wide-band-gap semiconductors are leading platforms for solid-state quantum technologies, yet a quantitative description of their vibronic structure has remained elusive due to the complexity of multiphonon processes in localized defect states. Here we present a first-principles Green's function framework based on the retarded cumulant ansatz (RCA) to describe electron-phonon interactions in spin defects; our approach goes beyond the adiabatic and lowest-order perturbation theory approximations underlying widely used approaches. Applied to the negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy ( NV − ) center in diamond within the harmonic approximation, our method reveals that multiphonon satellites persist over a 400 meV energy window even at zero temperature, driven by quantum zero-point fluctuations. We demonstrate that accurate spectral functions require mode-, momentum-, spin-, and orbital-resolved electron-phonon matrix elements sampled across the full Brillouin zone, to account for hybridized and propagating phonon channels. We find that the vibronic structure of the NV − center exhibits strong spin and orbital anisotropy, with different orbitals coupling to qualitatively distinct parts of the phonon spectrum, and spin-selective coupling affecting both sideband positions and intensities.

journal_new.title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells
journal_new.abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

journal_new.title: High-fidelity state transfer in silicon-vacancy-phononic networks with closed mechanical subsystems
journal_new.abstract: Building on the alternating-waveguide closed-mechanical-subsystem architecture introduced by Kuzyk and Wang [], we develop a diamond phononic network that overcomes the coupling-hierarchy bottleneck in the implementation analyzed there. Beyond replacing nitrogen-vacancy centers with silicon-vacancy (SiV) centers, we independently engineer the two relevant couplings: Localized defect modes and strong SiV orbital-strain interaction enhance the spin-phonon coupling G , whereas cavity-waveguide engineering suppresses the cavity-waveguide coupling g . The resulting coupling hierarchy reverses that found in earlier physical implementations of closed-mechanical-subsystem networks and places the system in the G ≫ g regime required for direct state transfer. This hierarchy reversal qualitatively changes the appropriate control strategy from bichromatic Mølmer-Sørensen driving to a simple direct triple swap. Within our model, the resulting protocol enables state transfer with a fidelity of 0.999 on a microsecond timescale and remains robust against mechanical dissipation, spin dephasing, and finite thermal occupation. Our results establish a distinct route for scalable solid-state phononic quantum networks.
